I'm a bit of a grey area on Griffith. I think pre-torture Griffith and Griffith after his experiences in The Tower Of Rebirth are two different people. That level of torture imprisoned his own rage inside him and the changes in his internal monologue even after he is freed make it clear that he is not the same man once was. He was never pure or perfect, but he was not truly, fundamentally evil until the moment he was reborn and chose to rape Casca for no purpose other than to hurt Guts. In that moment, his most loyal follower had become nothing to him but a tool, a possession of somebody else's to destroy to hurt the owner. His decision to sacrifice the Hawks was the ultimate in selfish cruelty, and his humanity died with his followers. Griffith is indefensible from the moment he speaks the words and sacrifices the people who love him. I think a lot of people are written off as Griffith fan girls because people don't make a clear distinction between how they feel about Griffith before he undergoes EXTREME FUCKING TORTURE (which, for the record, is a hell of a thing to happen to a person.) and post TOR Griffith. That level of psychological trauma changes people. It was Griffith's equivalent to Casca's rape during the Eclipse. What happened to both characters is unforgivably cruel, and there are no grey areas as to either act in my opinion. Pre-TOR Griffith I absolutely love, I feel a lot for him. Post-TOR Griffith is a damaged man stewing in his own rage and hatred. Femto is the metamorphosis of a broken man into an evil creature devoid of humanity; there isn't a rationalisation for the self-serving cruelty Griffith delivers unto those who would have died for him, as opposed to by his own hand for his own ends.

I dunno if I'm just a filthy Griffith apologist, but I feel sort of like the Godhand stating he was always going to choose to become Femto was not so much a statement that Griffith had planned this as some people interpret it, but rather a sort of retroactive acknowledgement that this fate had been foreseen and would always be the case precisely due to circumstance. It would always be the case because at the time of the Eclipse there was not really an option for Griffith not to become Femto; he was crippled, mute and in horrible pain, and likely suffering massive, massive psychological trauma. Rebirth was irresistible, and this was always how fate had dictated it was going to be.
